ai.description: *Mesalina brevirostris* (Lacertidae) reaches 5 cm snout-vent length. It is sandy-brown with distinct white dorsolateral stripes and a short, blunt snout. The tail is long and cylindrical.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Mesalina brevirostris* is best distinguished by its single, undivided prefrontal scale, whereas similar species typically possess two distinct prefrontal scales.
ai.habitat: *Mesalina brevirostris* inhabits arid, sandy, or gravelly deserts and semi-deserts with sparse xerophytic vegetation, typically found at low to moderate altitudes.
ai.behavior: The Short-snouted Sand Lizard is a diurnal forager that actively hunts small insects across sandy desert substrates during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Mesalina brevirostris* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally from spring through early summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Mesalina brevirostris* is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, specifically across Rajasthan and Gujarat, typically in sandy, low-elevation desert habitats.
